To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The use of concepts in query-based topic detection is a promising approach, 2) the use of named entities in the query improves the quality of the results and 3) the use of concepts in the query improves results for topics that are more general and for topics with a more complex structure.

the use of named entities and concepts improves the performance of query-based topic detection in the context of the CLEF 2016 QA@CLEF Task 1, and that a combination of named entities, concepts and keywords performs best.
The use of named entities, concepts and their co-occurrence patterns in query logs is a good way to detect topics in query logs.
